title: Fast developer path to SLA and cost anchors
summary: Messaging brief to position Redwood Hosted API for engineering teams who need a fast path from PoC to production with predictable economics and SLA-minded defaults. Includes quickstart flows, pricing language drafts, competitive rebuttals, and measurement plan.
content:
Objective:
- Craft a concise, developer-centric messaging and onboarding experience that reduces time-to-first-meaningful-call while surfacing cost controls and SLA options early in the flow.
- Produce copy and experiments that convert engineers into trial users who can validate a small-scope integration within 30–60 minutes and understand how to scale with committed capacity.

Primary audience:
- Backend engineers and ML engineers building assistants, search augmentation, summarization, or classification features.
- Platform engineers evaluating inference economics and SLA guarantees for product teams.
- Startup founders/CTOs who want production-ready inference without the ops overhead.

Core positioning pillars (developer-facing):
1) Start in minutes, predict at scale — one SDK, predictable economics, SLA path when you need it.
2) Production-first primitives — built-in batching, KV caching, and fallback routing so PoC behavior maps to prod.
3) Cost controls by default — meter, simulate, and cap before you pay; clear per-token and per-embedding anchors.
4) Same API across Hosted / Dedicated / Private — move from trial to commit without code rewrites.

One-line value props (for hero and microcopy):
- "Ship LLM features fast. Keep latency low, cost predictable, and scaling simple."
- "From first call to SLA-backed throughput — same API, clear economics."

Quickstart flows (3 parallel flavors to meet different buyer contexts):
A) 30-minute engineer quick-check (lowest friction)
- Goal: Make a single successful API call with a realistic prompt and view tokens + cost.
- Steps: sign up -> create API key -> run curl snippet (example included) -> view response stream -> see cost estimator in console.
- Success metric: call completed + cost estimate visible within 30m.
- Example microcopy for curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"rwd-small-1","input":"Summarize: <paste text>"}'

B) 1-hour integration (prototype to demo):
- Goal: Integrate hosted API into a small service endpoint (e.g., slackbot or search augmentation).
- Steps: install SDK, implement retry/backoff helper, enable prefix caching for repeated user prompts, add basic usage alert and token cap.
- Success metric: working demo plus usage alert triggered once during stress test.

C) Platform validation (ops + cost readout):
- Goal: Validate predictable token cost under expected traffic and identify when to switch to Dedicated.
- Steps: run a 10k-request load profile, check per-token latency percentiles, simulate autoscaling bursts, review recommended batching/quantization suggestions from Optimize.
- Success metric: predicted monthly cost within 15% of measured; latency p95 within SLO.

Suggested pricing-language drafts (tone: transparent, engineer-respectful):
- Headline: "Pay for what you use. Trade to reserved capacity as you commit."
- Per-token example: "Generative calls: $0.002 per 1,000 tokens (text-gen-std). Embeddings: $0.0008 per 1k embedding units."
- Starter credits: "New accounts get $250 in credits for 30 days to experiment end-to-end."
- Predictability path: "When you need guaranteed throughput and lower unit cost, choose Dedicated: monthly committed throughput with SLA-backed latency."
- Cost-control primitives to advertise early: token caps, rate limits, billing alerts, model routing to cheaper variants, and simulated monthly estimators in the console.

Snippets for onboarding microcopy (signup, console, billing):
- Signup CTA: "Try inference — $250 credit, no CC for 14 days" (or server-side AB test with CC vs no-CC).
- Console banner on first project: "Estimate your monthly cost with real sample prompts — try the cost simulator"
- Billing FAQ line: "Tokens are counted per-call (input+output). We show a live estimate in the console and send alerts if projected spend exceeds your cap."

Competitive notes and quick rebuttals:
- vs Big cloud vendor managed endpoints: 
  - Claim: They have broad infra but slower dev workflows and higher op area fragmentation.
  - Rebuttal: Redwood offers a focused dev API with first-class inference primitives (KV prefix caching, continuous batching) and explicit cost recommendations — fewer surprises migrating to production.
- vs LLM API-only incumbents focused on model breadth: 
  - Claim: They emphasize model catalog and features, less on cost predictability.
  - Rebuttal: Our messaging should emphasize economic controls and the predictable path to SLA-backed Dedicated capacity.
- vs DIY self-hosted inference stacks: 
  - Claim: More control and potentially lower cost at scale.
  - Rebuttal: Highlight time-to-value: weeks saved, operational complexity avoided, and transparent unit economics that allow teams to decide when (and whether) to self-host.

Launch experiments (A/B tests to run in next 6 weeks):
1) Signup CTA language: "$250 credit / no CC" vs "$250 credit / CC required" — conversion and retention delta.
2) Pricing anchor display: show per-token vs dollar-per-feature (e.g., cost per search result) — measure comprehension and intent to upgrade.
3) Quickstart hero: "30s curl test" vs "1-click SDK sample app" — which increases time-to-first-call and retention.

Measurement and success metrics (GTM + product):
- Time to first successful call (median) per new account.
- % of accounts that run the cost simulator within 24h.
- Trial-to-paid conversion rate for teams that run the 1-hour integration flow.
- NAC (new active customers) that hit threshold for Dedicated evaluation within 60 days.
- Average cost predictability error: abs(predicted_monthly_cost - actual)/predicted.

Objections & prepared responses (sales/SE snippets):
- "We need guaranteed latency — can Hosted meet that?" -> "Hosted gives latency SLAs for committed plans; for early validation, we provide p95 telemetry and routing to a higher-performance variant with predictable tails."
- "How will costs scale?" -> "We provide a clear per-token model, a cost simulator, and autosuggested batching/quantization profiles to show estimated savings before you change runtime configs."
- "What if model outputs degrade after a quantized or cheaper variant?" -> "We surface quality regressions with evaluation runs tied to your prompt set and provide rollback policies and automatic fallbacks to higher-quality variants."

Content for a short one-pager to hand engineers (bullet format):
- 3-step demo: 1) Create API key, 2) Run curl example, 3) Inspect cost & latency in console.
- Dev-friendly features: streaming, function-like structured responses, SDKs (Python/Node/Go), example apps.
- Ops-friendly features: token caps, per-route quotas, model pinning, and canary rollouts.
- Next recommended actions: try the 30-minute demo; schedule a platform review if you expect sustained traffic > 25k calls/day.

Next steps (who does what):
- GTM: implement A/B tests for signup CTA and quickstart hero (owner: Asha V.).
- Product: expose a single-click cost simulator in the project home and add recommended token caps after first call (owner: Rafael O.).
- DevRel: create the 30-minute tutorial repo and two short videos (30s curl + 7m integration) (owner: Maya T.).
- Metrics: instrument "time_to_first_call" and "cost_simulator_used" events (owner: Analytics).

Notes/tone guidance for copywriters:
- Keep tone concise and technical-friendly; avoid marketing fluff. Engineers should be able to find a runnable example in <60s and a meaningful cost estimate in <30m.
- Use concrete numbers/examples rather than vague promises.
- Surface ops controls early — engineers judge platforms by what they can configure.

Appendix: quick curl example (copyable)
- curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-infer-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize: The quarterly report showed growth in X..."}],"max_tokens":256}'

End of brief.
